For applicability, [78070,78175) records the resulting 31ba1a5 build commit and [78398,78461) records the successful main-to-main update 3027e0c..31ba1a5 in license-list-data. The two annotated tag targets independently identify the observed source and destination revisions within the SPDX lineage. The cited passages document deployment context for the inspected file.

challenge.method: Compared the XML fields directly to the generated JSON, then tested three possible errors separately: a reference to another publisher tool or to a deed, a tag pointing to a different revision, and matching release labels without evidence of actual generation.
challenge.results: The publisher's edition path and the explicit legalcode suffix resolve the instrument and representation being referenced. Both tag targets match the respective inspected file pins. The job's checked-out full SHA, source-to-output generator command, generated commit message and push agree with the separate Git objects, including both ends of the push. This supports the causal lineage for the bounded JSON record.

limitations: The XML, generated JSON, tags, commit and job carry the corresponding SPDX information lineage. They document release attribution and generation within that lineage. Both tags and the generated commit are unsigned.
The crosswalk concerns the identified file at the specified release. It establishes neither representation equivalence nor a copyright classification or project-specific grant.
The job records a build using additional inputs, including live URL checks. No independent bit-for-bit build reproduction was performed.
The fixed source reported the entire 81,691-byte job body. The displayed output elided a middle portion. All six cited passages and the generator invocation were visible.
reasoning: The pinned generated JSON records CC0-1.0, the name “Creative Commons Zero v1.0 Universal”, and https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/legalcode. The pinned source XML has exactly the same identifier, name and URL. Creative Commons identifies that URL's zero/1.0 edition independently. The two annotated tags establish which revisions SPDX attributed to v3.29.0. The deployment record connects the actual XML checkout and generator invocation to the pushed data commit containing the inspected JSON.
